thread:
Sarah (Acme): Hey team — live streaming responses are coming back truncated for us. We see content but the stream closes before the final chunk. No finish_reason. Repro steps below.

Maya (support): Sorry about that, can you paste the raw curl you used and any request ids?

Sarah (Acme): Sure. Using the hosted API:
```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate \
  -d '{"model":"rw-large-2025","input":"Summarize the doc","stream":true}'
```
Stream output looks like: 
```
data: {"id":"resp_abc123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Here is the sum"},"finish_reason":null}]}
data: {"id":"resp_abc123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"mary of the"},"finish_reason":null}]}
# then connection drops. No final JSON with finish_reason:"stop" or data: [DONE]
```

Maya (support): Thanks. Any request id in headers or logs? Also did you see a 200 then EOF or an interim 5xx?

Sarah (Acme): Client only got a 200 and then socket close. No 5xx. We retried and sometimes get full stream but the failures are ~1 in 6 attempts.

ci-bot: New log entry: trace_id=trc_0f78a9 path=/v1/streams/generate latency=1223ms upstream_status=200 upstream_len=1789 socket_closed_by=peer

Jamal (eng-oncall): Jumping in — looks like socket_closed_by=peer. That usually means the client or an intervening proxy closed the connection. Two quick asks: (1) can you reproduce with a direct curl run from a different network (eg laptop vs corp VPN)? (2) can you collect tcpdump / packet trace if possible?

Sarah (Acme): Reproduced from home network (same behavior). I can run tcpdump if you tell me what to capture.

Lin (devex): A couple of things we've seen: some client EventSource polyfills/HTTP clients don't handle long-lived chunked responses and close on timeout. Also some load balancers cut idle connections ~60s. Do you see gaps in the stream prior to drop?

Sarah (Acme): The last partial chunk arrives within 1s of previous chunks, then immediate FIN. No long idle.

Maya (support): Thanks. Jamal / eng — can we check the edge logs for that trace_id and verify we flushed the final close event (we usually send final JSON with finish_reason or `data: [DONE]`)?

Jamal (eng-oncall): Looking at internal logs for trace_id trc_0f78a9: upstream svc reported full payload generated. At HTTP layer we see chunked transfer; however the connection shows TLS session closed by peer at ~1225ms before chunk flush of final 140 bytes. That suggests client closed before we finished writing. Need to correlate with downstream LB timeouts.

Maya (support): Sarah — what's your client library? Are you using an EventSource wrapper or raw curl?

Sarah (Acme): Our prod client is a Node fetch-based streamer using AbortController to enforce per-request timeout of 2s. For testing I was using curl without timeouts. We did have an internal watchdog that aborts if overall generation >1.1s.

Lin (devex): That is likely it — if your app aborts the fetch while the server is still sending the final chunk, you will see truncated output and no finish_reason. Two mitigation suggestions: (1) remove/extend the client abort timeout while debugging, (2) enable server-side keepalive heartbeats or expect the server to send periodic `data: "\n"` (we have a Keepalive option in SDKs).

Sarah (Acme): Interesting — but we still reproduce with curl (no abort) occasionally. Could there be a middlebox issue?

Jamal (eng-oncall): Possible. Next steps I recommend: (A) we capture a pcap from your client side when reproducing (tcpdump -w stream.pcap port 443), (B) we enable debug logging on our edge for trace_id so we can see exact bytes written, (C) try the same curl from a different AS/ISP and from our support subnet (we can provide a host).

Sarah (Acme): I'll run tcpdump now when it next happens. Also can you confirm billing/auth could cause sudden closes (we had a billing alert yesterday)?

billing-bot: Account Acme flagged for exceeded free-tier. Requests are still authorized but rate-limited.

Maya (support): Billing note: their account was rate-limited to a lower QPS but not outright rejected. That should not cause the connection to close mid-stream — the API returns 429 early if we rate limit.

Jamal (eng-oncall): Agreed. We should also rule out upstream OOM / worker termination: I'll grep runtime logs for any SIGTERM or worker restart around that timestamp.

ci-bot: runtime.log: [2026-03-14T18:12:03Z] worker=wv-12 pid=2381 oom_kill=false shutting_down=false last_write=1224ms

Jamal (eng-oncall): No OOM. Not seeing server-initiated kill. Looks client-initiated. Still we should harden server: ensure final event is flushed with force_flush() and continue sending small keepalive bytes until flush confirmed by kernel. I'll open an eng-runtime issue.

Lin (devex): Practical workaround for you, Sarah: add this HTTP header in client reconnects: `Last-Event-ID: <last_chunk_id>` and have the client reconnect on socket close to resume. Our streaming API supports idempotent resume for some models (we'll confirm supported model). Also set `Connection: keep-alive` and disable aggressive client timeouts.

Sarah (Acme): Ok will try. Quick question — what should we put in the Last-Event-ID? The `id` from the streamed JSON?

Maya (support): Yes, Last-Event-ID should match the `id` field when we include it in stream events. If you can't extract it, reconnecting with the same input will usually produce a new stream; client-side dedupe is best-effort.

Jamal (eng-oncall): I've created ENG-1897 to add stronger flush and heartbeat on the runtime side. Assigning to runtime team for patch and adding extra logging for chunk flush state.

Maya (support): For the customer: can you (1) test removing the AbortController timeout, (2) run curl from a different network and capture a pcap if it fails, (3) enable a client-side reconnect-on-close that retries once and sets Last-Event-ID = last seen id. Ping here with pcap and a new trace_id if it recurs.

Sarah (Acme): Will do. Appreciate the quick triage. I'll upload pcap + trace when I have it.

Maya (support): Thanks — marking P1 and escalating to eng-runtime. We'll follow up in ENG-1897 and loop back here when we have a runtime patch or more logs. :thumbsup:
